notes: Research draft, not wired into the app. Sources inherited from the recommendation and first-government research retain their original access dates; newly retrieved sources were read on 2026-11-05.

The term window runs from this election to the next Knesset election. Government tenure may extend past that window. Mid-term institutional succession is recorded in formation.events; it is not a new post-election recommendation round.

Additional dated mid-term acts that do not fit the proposal’s closed formation type vocabulary are kept as formalStep=true entries in government.changes (Dated-compatible). No new formation enum values are introduced.

The endedBy date anchors the President’s 27 October notice, not the later statutory dissolution. IPU’s 10 November dissolution claim is rejected: the Basic Law route follows the 21-day period under sections 10–11, not a dissolution law. No exact later notice date is inferred from statutory arithmetic.

cites.quote: קצב ציין, כי 78 מחברי הכנסת הבאה תמכו במועמדותו של אולמרט בסבב ההתייעצויות, שקיים עם הסיעות וזאת ללא התנגדות, או המלצה על מועמד אחר. קצב הבהיר, כי יו"ר העבודה, עמיר פרץ הודיע לו טלפונית שלשום בערב, כי גם סיעת העבודה מעבירה את תמיכתה לאולמרט.

Kadima, Labor, Shas and the Pensioners’ Party all endorsed Olmert. UTJ is expected to endorse him as well. National Union-NRP initially endorsed Peretz, until it became clear that he did not really intend to pursue the position. Likud, Yisrael Beiteinu and all three Arab parties declined to endorse anybody.
Meretz has recommended Ehud Olmert as candidate for prime minister in a meeting with President Moshe Katsav Monday.
Shas members recommended Olmert for prime minister.
הרב אליישיב הורה לנציגים החרדים בסיעה להמליץ באוזני הנשיא על אולמרט.
אולמרט - 78 פירוט: קדימה 29, העבודה 19, ש"ס 12, גיל 7, יהדות התורה 6 ומרצ 5.

notes: Consultations ran 2–6 April 2006; Olmert was given the mandate on 6 April. Labor first recommended Amir Peretz (2 April) and transferred its support to Olmert by phone on 4 April; the President counted it in his 78. The National Union–NRP did not recommend anyone at its meeting and asked for more time (Ynet); INN says it 'initially endorsed Peretz' — a source conflict; the President's final statement records no other candidate. No contemporary report of UTJ's own meeting with the President was retrieved: its 6 follow from the President's 78 total less the five other recommending lists (72) and match the Hebrew Wikipedia breakdown.

Final positions as of 6 April. Labor initially recommended Peretz on 2 April, then transferred support to Olmert on 4 April; the final tally must not be presented as the initial consultation positions.
